name: Prisma Postgres
tagline: Serverless Postgres from the Prisma ORM team, on unikernels, billed per operation with no cold starts.
description: Prisma Postgres is a managed PostgreSQL service from Prisma, the company behind the popular TypeScript ORM. It runs each database in lightweight unikernel microVMs on bare metal, which lets it pack many databases densely and avoid the cold starts of scale-to-zero designs. Billing counts operations (queries) and storage rather than compute hours, and the service includes connection pooling and optional global query caching. It became generally available in 2025 and now accepts direct TCP connections from any Postgres client, not just the Prisma ORM. It is an easy default for TypeScript teams already on Prisma; check operation-based pricing against heavy, chatty workloads before committing.

pricing.notes: Free: 200k operations/month, 50 databases, small storage allowance. Starter: 1M operations then $8/M, 10 GB then $2/GB. Pro and Business tiers above.

scale.notes: Single-primary databases; global caching can serve reads near users.

strengths: Unikernel architecture avoids cold starts while keeping per-database cost low
Tight integration with Prisma ORM, Migrate and Studio
Simple operation-based pricing with a free tier
Built-in connection pooling and optional query caching
Standard Postgres TCP connections for non-Prisma tools
weaknesses: Young service with a limited extension list
Operation-based billing can be costly for chatty ORMs or batch jobs
No branching, read scaling or multi-region writes
Vendor is best known for an ORM, not database operations
useCases: TypeScript apps built with Prisma ORM
Side projects and startups needing quick Postgres
Serverless functions on Vercel, Netlify or Cloudflare
Many small databases for templates or AI-generated apps
